contract.observation: Revision 2 was frozen before the corrected replay. Revision 1 remains physically preserved and is linked by the oracle-correction evidence.

initialObservations.finding: G05 was malformed before semantic binding and G06 used an unknown seed field; both were corrected under the independent oracle-review record.

focusedReplay.coverage: The permanent matrix runs 48 frozen invalid candidates across eight six-case families, verifies exact diagnostic sequences and locations, repeats multi-root analysis for stable source order, and checks that repairing one root leaves exactly the next genuine root.

productionFindings.description: Diagnostic recovery either stopped independent siblings or allowed derivative callable, set-output, recursive-shape and aggregate semantic noise to obscure the genuine root.
productionFindings.repair: Keep the semantic stack balanced after an unresolved callable, suppress only dependent callable failures, carry poisoned set and recursive outputs through their owning root, and suppress non-aggregated projection noise for poisoned expressions while retaining independent roots.

obligations.REC-123-O01: The 48-case matrix covers projections, aggregates, windows, casts, set outputs, recursive members and interpretation fields.
obligations.REC-123-O02: Exact diagnostic-code assertions reject derivative member, cast, callable and type noise after the root failure.
obligations.REC-123-O03: Repeated analysis compares code, span and message tuples and requires nondecreasing source offsets for every multi-root case.
obligations.REC-123-O04: The repair trajectory changes missing.Name to a valid Name and asserts that only the remaining Unknown column root survives.
obligations.acceptance: The matrix detects both over-reporting and over-suppression without accepting an intended code anywhere in an unbounded cascade.

notes: The revision-1 contract, manifest and replay artifacts remain preserved; the corrected revision-2 contract was independently reviewed before replay.
